'Not checkpointed' is part of GAP-A1-02. Its planned closing unit (G4 with FindingState, OPEN-ITEMS OI-77) was not built and its design is ruled stale (H-A1-1).

REPAIR-EQUIVALENCE-001.notes: A1b (TRACED, AUTH-A1-04): since the row was written, a repeated candidate is detected after its gates ran (same effective workspace bytes or a repeated progress vector count toward the no-progress stop; strategy changes after 2, the unit stops at 3). What the row still asks for, refusing a byte-identical candidate before a gate round, is not built: an efficiency capability, consistent with the registry's DEFERRED. Not replayed against the S3_A recording. Disposition is a proposal.

SEMANTIC-SAFETY-REPAIR-CONTINUITY-001.notes: A1b (MEASURED, probe P10): the staging rejection is kept as the open finding with its prohibition text and survives a resource refusal; it is replaced, and the prohibition leaves the open set, on the next candidate finding of any kind and on a no_progress_retry refusal. Same root as GAP-A1-01 (one-element open set, no blocker lifecycle) and GAP-A1-07. The row's second claim (the message does not say the edit was not applied) was not checked: prompt wording, slice A4. Disposition is a proposal and follows GAP-A1-01.

ATTEMPT-ATOMIC-CANDIDATE-DISCARDS-VALID-.notes: A1b (TRACED): confirmed as current behaviour and as a stated contract of workflow/candidate_transaction.py ('the first refusal raises and refuses the whole attempt; nothing staged'). The measured consequence (a valid edit for the blamed file is refused with its sibling's protocol failure) stands. Whether attempt atomicity is the intended contract or a defect is not decided by evidence in A1: carried to slice A3 (candidate transaction) and Phase B for the disposition.

TRIAGE-ON-ORCHESTRATOR-NOTICE-001.notes: A1b (TRACED): still current at the call site. retry_strategy._record_attempt_failure sets environment_failure for time_budget_exhausted and then calls attribution.attribute_failure without a guard on that stop, and a search of workflow/attribution.py found no orchestrator or time-budget exclusion. The ladder's own tiers are traced in slice A2; disposition in Phase B.

RETRY-REFERENCE-CONTEXT-DEDUP-001.notes: A1b: not re-measured (the registry row is MEASURED on run 10 and records the reverted attempt). Part of GAP-A1-03 (attempt accounting in evidence). Disposition with the evidence schema in slice A6 / Phase B.

Missing evidence, exactly: a deterministic resume of a unit from that checkpoint in human-in-the-loop mode with deferred gates. The registry's own W3-8 disposition (2026-11-01) split the row: the effect-ownership half is fixed and verified (3e1df0c); what remains is stale Docker proxy and network objects after a SIGKILL, measured safe on 2026-09-29 (no adoption, reuse, contamination or false success), routed to an operations-hardening pass with the owner's approved deferral. No retry, authority or result-truth question. Process and container ownership is mapped in slice A5. Disposition is a proposal.

GUI-RECOVERY-ACTION-001.notes: A1b (TRACED): the kernel recovery action exists (kriya/cli_commands/runs.py runs_recover, named by the typed blocker in cli.py). The desktop has no button for it. The state is typed and safe; the registry already classifies it a future capability.

RECOVERY-UPSTREAM-OWNER-ROUTING-001.notes: A1b (TRACED): the stop this row observed was changed on 2026-11-11 (ATTRIBUTION-MODEL-CLAIM-HARD-STOP-001): NO_AUTHORIZED_REPAIR_TARGET now requires a deterministic attribution tier, and a deterministic tier naming only out-of-scope files is claimed first by the plan-scope escalation, which routes to owner recovery. If the 2026-10-10 stop came from an advisory tier the row is stale; that cannot be decided without the tier of that run's attribution. Missing evidence, exactly: the attribution tier of unit s2 in C2-S4_A-c3 (its sealed store). Owned by slice A2 (attribution).

RECOVERY-MAY-CHANGE-ANSWERED-NO-CHANGE-R.notes: A1b (TRACED, FR-A1-20): confirmed. The enforce loop accepts 'legitimately unchanged' only as the unit's typed VERIFICATION_RETRY_NO_CHANGE_POSSIBLE stop with equal bytes; any other answer fails the group and the recovery. Safe failure. The unit-side settlement (workflow.py, verified_no_change.py) is traced in slice A3; disposition in Phase B.

ENFORCE-UPSTREAM-WORK-PRESERVATION-001.notes: A1b (TRACED + MEASURED): confirmed and made GAP-A1-09. The discard is the deliberate consequence of two contracts (atomic terminal commit; sandbox completions are not resumable). Whether accepted unit state may be preserved for review or resume without being committed is a product-policy choice the row has asked for since 2026-10-09: an owner decision (Phase D item O) unless Phase B evidence decides it.

CROSS-UNIT-PRODUCER-RECOVERY-CAPABILITY-.notes: A1b (TRACED, SM-A1-04, FR-A1-22): consistent with the owner's disposition of 2026-11-06. Routes that exist: owner recovery when attribution grounds the failure to a completed owner's file, and the owner-reopen episode of a verification-only unit. A file-owning consumer whose behavioural failure is not grounded to an upstream file has no route and fails closed after bounded attempts.

GUI-TRACE-ATTEMPTS-SEMANTICS-001.notes: A1b (TRACED): confirmed. workflow/run_lifecycle.py writes runs.attempts = retry_count + best_of_n_candidates_tried (the full-set counter, not attempts made) and workflow/run_trace.py writes 0 on early exits. Part of GAP-A1-03. Disposition with the evidence schema in slice A6 / Phase B.

KERNEL-RESULT-RUNID-DIVERGES-001.notes: A1b (TRACED): confirmed in part and by construction. A unit result's run_id is the trace id (workflow.py: trace_id_override or an 8-hex id), while its checkpoint id comes from control/checkpoint.py new_run_id (timestamp plus 8 hex) and is what retry_state_reference names; a checkpoint also stores a separate reference to its run record. So one unit invocation has at least two, probably three, identifiers with no single owner. The run-record side is traced with evidence identity in slice A6; disposition in Phase B.

GUI-EXEC-STOP-001.notes: A1b: consistent with the owner decision of 2026-10-10 (no Stop in v1). Kernel fact relevant to it (TRACED, FR-A1-15): a cancellation is not recorded as an attempt failure and no retry state survives it; whether an interrupt at every phase leaves a recoverable state is not established, which is the precondition the row itself names.
